generation.domain: nonsingular real linear system; no exchanges; integer entries

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & -2 & -4 & -4 \\ -2 & -4 & 0 & -20 \\ 1 & -1 & 8 & -18\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & -2 & -4 & -4 \\ -2 & -4 & 0 & -20 \\ 1 & -1 & 8 & -18\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 2 \\ -2 & -4 & 0 & -20 \\ 1 & -1 & 8 & -18\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 4 & -16 \\ 1 & -1 & 8 & -18\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 4 & -16 \\ 0 & -2 & 6 & -20\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=-\frac{1}{2}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 8 \\ 0 & -2 & 6 & -20\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y+2z&=2 \\ y-2z&=8 \\ z&=-2\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=-2 \\ y&=8-(-2)(-2)=4 \\ x&=2-(1)(4)-(2)(-2)=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 2,4,-2\rangle$.

$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & 3 & 3 & 0 \\ -2 & 5 & -1 & -21 \\ 2 & -4 & -2 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{3}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 5 & -1 & -21 \\ 2 & -4 & -2 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -21 \\ 2 & -4 & -2 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 & -21 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=\frac{1}{3}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -7 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -7 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y-z&=0 \\ y-z&=-7 \\ z&=4\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=4 \\ y&=-7-(-1)(4)=-3 \\ x&=0-(-1)(-3)-(-1)(4)=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 1,-3,4\rangle$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+4y-4z&=8 \\ -x-4y-2z&=-6 \\ x+4y-z&=0\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 4 & -4 & 8 \\ -1 & -4 & -2 & -6 \\ 1 & 4 & -1 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ -1 & -4 & -2 & -6 \\ 1 & 4 & -1 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & -2 \\ 1 & 4 & -1 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & -4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=-\frac{1}{2}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & -4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & -6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-2z&=4 \\ y+2z&=1 \\ z&=2\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=2 \\ y&=1-(2)(2)=-3 \\ x&=4-(2)(-3)-(-2)(2)=14.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 14,-3,2\rangle$.

$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & 6 & 0 & -9 \\ 1 & -4 & 4 & -5 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{3}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & -4 & 4 & -5 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 4 & -8 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 4 & -8 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 & 5\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=-\frac{1}{2}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 & 5\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=\frac{1}{3}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y&=3 \\ y-2z&=4 \\ z&=-1\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=-1 \\ y&=4-(-2)(-1)=2 \\ x&=3-(-2)(2)-(0)(-1)=7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 7,2,-1\rangle$.

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & 2 & -2 & 6 \\ -2 & 0 & -4 & 14 \\ -1 & 2 & -3 & -4\end{array}\right].

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & 8 \\ -1 & 2 & -3 & -4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -7\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=-\frac{1}{2}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -7\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_2$, we obtain

$$

$$

$$

M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -3 & -3 & -6 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 & 8 \\ -2 & 0 & 3 & -12\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 & 8 \\ -2 & 0 & 3 & -12\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 4 \\ -2 & 0 & 3 & -12\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & -16\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=\frac{1}{2}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & -16\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & -12\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y-z&=-2 \\ y-2z&=2 \\ z&=4\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=4 \\ y&=2-(-2)(4)=10 \\ x&=-2-(-1)(10)-(-1)(4)=12.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 12,10,4\rangle$.

knowledge_point.title: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination

generation.domain: nonsingular real linear system; no exchanges; integer entries

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-3x+6y-6z&=-12 \\ x+2z&=2 \\ -2x+5y-6z&=-3\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & 6 & -6 & -12 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ -2 & 5 & -6 & -3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{3}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ -2 & 5 & -6 & -3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ -2 & 5 & -6 & -3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 5\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=\frac{1}{2}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 5\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y+2z&=4 \\ y&=-1 \\ z&=-3\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=-3 \\ y&=-1-(0)(-3)=-1 \\ x&=4-(-2)(-1)-(2)(-3)=8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 8,-1,-3\rangle$.
